claims.title: Thermal-core capacity and finite weighted sparse-entrance current

quoted_fields.interface: Periodic L by L torus; n=L^2, theta>=4, phi=theta/R; actual per-site heatbath rates and fixed zero-coupling contour diagonals. A=C_r is the acquired thermal core and B={M>=0}. Require r>=1, r+2<=R/3, r<L/4 and the original source-edge convention, including A intersect B, with actual kappa>0. The sparse corollary additionally requires acquired Z_M5/Z_A<=1/(1-u_r), u_r<1, K=floor(5R^2), M<K+1 and embedded nonwinding filled domains.
quoted_fields.failure: The negligible quantity is weighted current through the specified sparse entrance configurations, not the probability of every transition path containing one. Dense, winding and other entrances, physical growth/residence composition and the full transition mean remain open. The core-size and source convention are indispensable; finite examples violating them are rejected. Normalized capacity/thermal transport and Thomson methods pre-exist, and the coarse finite exponent does not improve the cited sharp asymptotic exponent. New proofs are internally derived and not independently verified. Existing N1722 scientific acceptances retain their own versions and full scope; no older result is downgraded or replaced.
